transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
Former Congresswoman Mary Peltola is the next senator from Alaska.
According to an AP race call, Peltola has flipped the Senate seat held by Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan.
I'm so grateful you've put your trust in me, Alaska, and I'm ready to get to work.
The future is full of opportunities for us to make Alaska a better place across the state.
I'm looking forward to working hand-in-hand with all Alaskans over the next six years.
Thank you again.
Peltola is speaking in a social media video posted Tuesday night.
Her victory gives Democrats a 56 to 44 seat majority when the new Congress meets in January.
Democrats also celebrating a victory in North Carolina,
where Raymond Smith has defeated Republican Congressman Greg Murphy in a tight House race.
NPR's Hansi Luong reports on that race call by the AP.
Former Democratic state lawmaker Raymond Smith flipped North Carolina's third congressional district with just a few hundred votes.
And I'll stand up to anybody and any party who sails out the working people of eastern North Carolina.
Smith's victory brings a total number of black members of the U.S. House to at least 61.
That's according to an NPR analysis of the latest AP race calls, and that's down from 63 currently.
It's also just too away from the record loss of four black representatives around the end of Reconstruction.
Some redistricting experts warn that in the coming years,
more black-represented districts may be eliminated when voting maps are redrawn
because of the Supreme Court's weakening of the Voting Rights Act's protections against racial discrimination in redistricting.
Hansi Luong, NPR News.
New York Attorney General Letitia James has formally challenged the revised petition to remove her from the Cornell rape investigation.
Ellie Oskara with member station WAMC reports.
In a memo filed Monday in state Supreme Court, attorneys representing the attorney general pushed back against a petition
signed by five students accused of sexual assault in the 2024 incident at Cornell University.
The petition revolves around a social media post.
James wrote, saying, quote, "What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable."
The state's memo argues the petition still has flaws.
Namely, other defendants in the Jane Doe litigation were left out of the petition, but could still be found criminally liable.
They also argued that since Jane Doe's case is in Tompkins County, the petition should be filed there instead of Albany County.
For NPR News, I'm Elias Oskara.
President Trump says he's concluded what he calls a very big trade deal with the Philippines during a state luncheon at the Philippine Presidential Palace.
Trump said it's a fair deal for both countries, but he did not provide any details.
And there's been no comment from the Philippine president.
Trump is to travel on to China, where he plans to meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.
You're listening to NPR News.
Secretary of State Marco Rubio was seeking to reassure the American public about the spate of tech issues that have led to snarled airports and affected banking, national security and email.
We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind.
Again, we have no evidence of that. We have no indications of that. We have no reason to believe that.
Rubio speaking to reporters while in the Philippines with President Trump.
There were a couple more tech outages Tuesday reported by Apple and Marriott, the nation's largest hotel operator.
After NASA launched it almost 50 years ago, the Voyager 1 probe documented the planets and eventually left the solar system.
Sandin Totten reports that the spacecraft is about to achieve another major milestone.
Early Wednesday morning, Voyager 1 will reach a distance of exactly one light day away from Earth.
A light day is how far light travels in just 24 hours. It's about 16 billion miles.
NASA scientist Linda Spilker worked on the project when it launched. She says over the last five decades, Voyager completely upended what we knew about space.
For me, it's not a surprise anymore that many of the things that Voyager is finding don't necessarily agree with the models that we have.
Voyager holds the record for the furthest any human-made object has traveled in space. Wednesday morning, it'll pass that light day mile marker, then plow forward into the unknown.
For NPR News, I'm Sandin Totten. And I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News.

topics.text: Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate seat from Dan Sullivan, flipping it per AP call
Raymond Smith defeats Republican Greg Murphy in North Carolina's third district House race
Black House representatives total drops to at least 61 amid redistricting and Voting Rights Act concerns
Letitia James formally challenges revised petition to remove her from Cornell rape investigation
Trump announces concluded trade deal with the Philippines during Manila luncheon, without details
Marco Rubio says no evidence tech outages are caused by hackers or hostile actors
Voyager 1 to reach one light day from Earth, a farther-than-ever distance milestone
